newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka president sacks minister in reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka president sacks minister in reshuffle.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga on Monday sacked her transport minister and brought eight new faces into her cabinet in the first reshuffle since her People's Alliance (PA) government took power in 1994.
Kumaratunga's new cabinet did not include Srimani Athulathmudali, leader of the PA constituent Democratic United National Lalith Front (DUNLF), who had held the transport job.
Political sources said Athulathmudali was sacked from the cabinet following recent sharp differences between DUNF and the government over policy matters.
Kumaratunga also changed the portfolios of some of her ministers in an attempt to ease workload and rationalise work, officials said.
The reshuffle raised Kumaratunga's cabinet strength to 31 from the earlier 23. The cabinet includes Prime Minister Srimavo Bandaranaike and Kumaratunga herself.

Kumaratunga kept the key finance and defence portfolios, but let go of an important religious ministry which handles Buddhist affairs. That portfolio was given to Lakshman Jayakody, the minister for cultural and religious affairs.
Sri Lanka is a predominantly Buddhist country and the clergy has traditionally played an important role in politics.
Foreign affairs stayed with Lakshman Kadirgamar. Both Bandaranaike and Kadirgamar are currently overseas.
Bandaranaike is in China for medical treatment and Kadirgamar is visiting London.
The state radio said the information portfolio was taken away from minister Dharmasiri Senanayake, leaving him with tourism and civil aviation.
Mangala Samarweera, a close confidant of Kumaratunga, was given the information ministry and kept his previous job as posts and telecommunications minister.

The government was recently embarrassed over its proposed Broadcast Bill, designed to curb the private radio and television stations by making it necessary for them to renew their licences each year and it was widely speculated that Senanayake's portfolios would be pruned.
The bill was shot down by the Supreme Court last month after it was challenged by various media organisations as well as the main opposition United National Party.
Labour Minister Mahinda Rajapakse, who was mostly seen as pro-labour by the business lobby, was shifted to fisheries and aquatic resources.
The labour portfolio went to new entrant John Seneviratne.
Athulathmudali's exit from the cabinet was widely expected after her DUNLF chose not to support the ruling coalition during local government elections in March.
The DUNLF said that the government was slow in implementing promises made during the 1994 parliamentary elections.
Health Minister Mohammed Fowzie was given Athulathmudali's transport and highways portfolios, while housing minister Nimal Siripala de Silva was shifted to health.
Kingsley Wickremaratne kept his internal and external trade portfolio while C.V.Gooneratne retained the post of industrial development.
Apart from Seneviratne, the new ministers are:

Hema Ratnayake - Women's Affairs; Alavi Moulana - Local Government and Provincial Councils; Maithripala Sirisena - Mahaveli Development; Jeyaraj Fernandopulle - Plan Implementation and Parliamentary Affairs; Berty Premalal Dissanayake - Social Services; Nandimithra Ekanayake - Forestry and Environment; D.P. Wickramasinghe - Cooperatives Development.
